newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler investing $1.3 billion in plants.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler investing $1.3 billion in plants.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Wednesday it will invest an additional $1.3 billion in the company's Detroit manufacturing facilities over the next five years.
The new spending will improve efficiency and potentially increase capacity, Chrysler said.
"This announcement translates directly into more jobs for Detroiters," Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer said in a statement released by Chrysler.
The investment will be spread over six Detroit facilities, the company said.

Chrysler said it will spend $750 million at the Jefferson-North Assembly Plant for a new body shop, an additional color spray booth and capacity increases, and $300 million at Detroit Axle for new model expansion, infrastructure improvements and capacity increases.

It said it will spend $150 million more at Mack Avenue Engine Plant for technological improvements and potential capacity increases, bringing the total investment in the yet-to-be-opened facility to $900 million.

Chysler said another $100 million will go to McGraw Glass for new model expansion and infrastructure improvements, $10 million for the introduction of the Plymouth Prowler at the Conner Avenue Assembly Plant, and $3 million for infrastructure improvements at Mt. Elliott Tool and Die.

"The new technologies being employed, processes being improved and the upgrading of the infrastructures in these Detroit facilities are designed to further improve the quality and cost of the new models being introduced by Chrysler in upcoming years," Chrysler chairman Robert Eaton said in a statement.
In a news conference, Eaton said the investments would create "hundreds of jobs", but he declined to give a specific number.

Eaton also declined to reveal the number of additional vehicles that Chrysler would be able to build as a result of the investments. Some analsyts have estimated that the expansion of the Jefferson-North Assemtbly Plant will allow Chrysler to boost straight-time production capacity of Jeep Grand Cherokee sport utility vehicles to about 375,000 from about 260,000.

Eaton said the ultimate production and employment increases associated with the investment would depend on the strength of the U.S. car and truck markets and demand for Chrysler's future product line.

Eaton said the investments, which do not represent a change from the company's $22.8 billion five-year product spending program, are a small step toward the company's goal of boosting its annual worldwide production capacity to four million vehicles. Chrysler built about 2.8 million vehicles in 1996.
"This is a commitment to our workers, our facilities and the City of Detroit," Eaton said.
The $1.3 billion in investments brings Chrysler's total investment in Detroit to $3.8 billion since the company rebuilt its Jefferson North Assembly Plant, which opened in 1992.
Chrysler said it has added 2,100 jobs in the city since 1994, when it added its third shift at the Jefferson North facility.
